fi-tetraodon-nigroviridis.title: Tetraodon nigroviridis
fi-tetraodon-nigroviridis.summary: The green spotted puffer, Tetraodon nigroviridis, is a widespread puffer from South and Southeast Asia, found in both brackish and fresh water. It is often confused with T. fluviatilis and T.…
rows: Relishes all kinds of shellfish, as well as worms and other live and frozen foods.
A widespread species, being found in India, Sri Lanka, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.
notes: Best kept in a heavily-planted setup with twisted roots and branches to provide additional cover, although soft-leaved plants may be chewed by the fish.
Leave some open spaces inbetween for swimming, as this is an active species.

fi-tetraodon-lineatus.title: Fahaka Puffer
fi-tetraodon-lineatus.summary: The fahaka puffer, Tetraodon lineatus, is a large freshwater puffer from lakes and rivers across northern and West Africa, reaching 43 cm. Also known as the Nile puffer, it was previously named T.…
rows: Usually kept singly (or a known pair when breeding)
Egypt, Kenya, Sudan, Senegal, Ghana, Gambia, Cameroon, Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Sierra Leone, Burkina Faso and Guinea Bissau.
notes: This is a freshwater puffer and does not require the addition of salt to its tank.
We suggest a sandy substrate with smooth rocks and driftwood pieces for decoration.

fi-tetraodon-pustulatus.title: Cross River Puffer
fi-tetraodon-pustulatus.summary: The Cross River pufferfish, Tetraodon pustulatus, is a puffer endemic to the Cross River basin of Nigeria and Cameroon. It lives in the moderately fast-flowing main channels and is assessed as…
rows: In nature, the Cross River Puffer should be considered primarily a molluscivore, though they also show opportunistic tendencies.
Endemic to the Cross River basin of Nigeria and Cameroon, though virtually all aquarium specimens are caught in Cameroon and exported via Nigeria.
notes: Due to the inquisitive nature of this species, the aquarium should be well decorated with bogwood, rocks and other forms of enrichment, though plenty of swimming space should still be afforded.
Tetraodon pustulatus does well in a planted aquarium and is seldom destructive towards plants.

fi-xenopterus-naritus.title: Avocado Puffer
fi-xenopterus-naritus.summary: The golden puffer, Xenopterus naritus, is a pufferfish from estuarine rivers in China, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia. Much of the available information describes it as a freshwater…
rows: Relishes all kinds of shellfish, as well as worms and other live and frozen foods.
China, Myanmar, Thailand, Vietnam and Indonesia.
notes: We suggest a sandy substrate, with smooth rocks and driftwood pieces for decoration.

fi-dichotomyctere-ocellatus.title: Figure Eight Puffer
fi-dichotomyctere-ocellatus.summary: A small, patterned puffer from rivers and estuaries of Cambodia, Malaysia and Borneo. It lives in fresh to slightly brackish water and is very sensitive to poor water quality.
rows: Nips the fins of slow or long-finned fish; often does best kept alone
Carnivore: snails and unshelled shellfish (crab legs, prawns) regularly to wear down its ever-growing teeth, plus worms and other frozen or live foods
Southeast Asia: lower Mekong (Cambodia), Peninsular Malaysia and Borneo; rivers and coastal waters
notes: Seriously Fish notes it tends to live longer with a little marine salt added.
Planted tank with roots and branches for cover, sand, and open swimming space; soft plants may be chewed.

fi-colomesus-asellus.title: South American Puffer (Amazon Puffer)
fi-colomesus-asellus.summary: A small, active freshwater puffer from the Amazon basin, also sold as the "SAP". It lives in groups, needs clean, well-oxygenated water, and must eat hard-shelled foods to keep its beak worn down.
rows: Not aggressive as such, but not a general community fish; best alone or with other river fish
Forms loose groups; buy 6 or more
Meaty foods with regular shelled invertebrates (snails, crab legs, cockles) to wear down its ever-growing teeth
Much of the Amazon basin (Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Ecuador); north to Guyana and Venezuela
notes: Intolerant of organic waste: keep up water changes and strong filtration.
A true freshwater puffer; it does not need brackish water.
